make.name: NIO
make.description: Chinese premium electric-car maker founded in 2014 and known for battery swapping (about 4,000 stations, mostly in China). It also runs the mass-market Onvo brand and the small-car Firefly brand. Its European sales have shrunk to a handful of cars in 2026.

models.name: EP9
models.description: Two-seat electric track car built for Nio by RML Group and unveiled in London in November 2016. It has one motor per wheel; only 16 were built (six sold to Nio investors) and none were registered for road use.

generations.name: EP9
generations.description: Carbon-fibre track car with four motors, one per wheel, and swappable batteries.

models.name: ES8
models.description: Nio's first production car: a full-size three-row SUV with swappable batteries, built in Hefei since June 2018. The second generation (2023) moved to the NT 2.0 platform and was sold in Europe as the EL8; the third generation launched in September 2025 on the 900-volt NT 3.0 platform and became Nio's best seller, with a five-seat version added in 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Aluminium-bodied six/seven-seat SUV with dual motors and swappable 70, 84 and later 100 kWh packs; revised in 2020 with a 160 kW front and 240 kW rear motor.

generations.name: Second generation (NT 2.0)
generations.description: All-new body on the NT 2.0 platform with lidar and the Adam computer; 75 or 100 kWh packs and a 480 kW dual-motor drive. Sold in Europe as the EL8.

generations.name: Third generation (NT 3.0)
generations.description: Larger 5.28 m body on the 900-volt NT 3.0 platform shared with the ET9, a 102 kWh pack and 520 kW dual motors; launched 20 September 2025.

models.name: ES6
models.description: Five-seat mid-size SUV with swappable batteries, on sale in China since June 2019. The second generation (2023, NT 2.0) is sold in Europe as the EL6 because Audi objected to the ES6 name; it was refreshed in May 2025 with an ET9-style interior.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Dual-motor SUV (permanent-magnet plus induction motor, up to 400 kW) with 70, 84 or 100 kWh swappable packs.

generations.name: Second generation (NT 2.0)
generations.description: Entirely new car on the NT 2.0 platform with 75 or 100 kWh packs; sold in Europe as the EL6.

generations.name: 2025 refresh
generations.description: May 2025 update with ET9-style styling, a landscape 15.6-inch screen and head-up display; powertrain carried over.

models.name: EC6
models.description: Coupe-roofed sister of the ES6, on sale in China since 2020 and built under contract by JAC. A second generation on NT 2.0 arrived in September 2023 and was refreshed in May 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Five-seat coupe SUV with 70 or 100 kWh swappable packs and two power levels.

generations.name: Second generation (NT 2.0)
generations.description: Launched 15 September 2023 on NT 2.0 with EC7-style body details and a 360 kW drive.

generations.name: 2025 refresh
generations.description: May 2025 update with ET9-style interior and landscape screen; powertrain carried over.

models.name: ET7
models.description: Large electric sedan and Nio's first car with lidar, unveiled in January 2021 and delivered from March 2022 in China and October 2022 in Europe. It was Nio's flagship until the ET9 and was updated in April 2024 with a new interior and an LFP standard-range pack.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launch version: 180 kW front and 300 kW rear motors, 75 kWh LFP/NMC hybrid or 100 kWh NMC packs.

generations.name: 2024 refresh
generations.description: April 2024 update: new rear executive seats and screens, Snapdragon 8295 cockpit, and an LFP 75 kWh pack with 170 kW charging; exterior almost unchanged.

models.name: ET5
models.description: Mid-size sedan aimed at the Tesla Model 3, revealed in December 2021 and on sale from September 2022. It was refreshed in May 2025 on the NT 2.5 platform.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Dual-motor sedan (150 kW front induction, 210 kW rear permanent-magnet) with 75 or 100 kWh swappable packs.

generations.name: 2025 refresh
generations.description: May 2025 update: adaptive headlights, landscape 15.6-inch screen, AR head-up display, Shenji chip; powertrain unchanged.

models.name: ET5 Touring
models.description: Estate version of the ET5, unveiled in June 2023 and sold in China as the ET5T. Same length and powertrain as the sedan, with a 470-litre boot; refreshed with the sedan in May 2025.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Wagon body on the ET5 platform with 75 or 100 kWh packs.

generations.name: 2025 refresh
generations.description: May 2025 update shared with the ET5 sedan; adds 1,400 kg towing.

models.name: ES7
models.description: Five-seat mid-size SUV, the first car on Nio's NT 2.0 platform (2022), sold in Europe as the EL7. Nio quietly stopped selling it in China in 2025 without an announcement; export production continues.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Dual-motor 480 kW SUV with 75 or 100 kWh swappable packs and an optional 2,000 kg tow bar.

models.name: EC7
models.description: Coupe-roofed sister of the ES7, announced at Nio Day 2022 with deliveries from mid-2023; Nio claims a 0.23 drag coefficient. Sales have been very small (1,258 in China in 2025).

generations.name: Original
generations.description: 180 kW front and 300 kW rear motors with 75 or 100 kWh swappable packs.

models.name: ET9
models.description: Nio's flagship four-seat executive sedan, the first on the 900-volt NT 3.0 platform with steer-by-wire, fully active suspension and Nio's own Shenji driving chips. Deliveries began in March 2025.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: 100 kWh pack with 600 kW charging, 180 kW front and 340 kW rear motors.

models.name: ES9
models.description: Full-size three-row flagship SUV, the SUV counterpart to the ET9, revealed in April 2026 with deliveries from June 2026.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: 102 kWh pack, 925-volt drive with 180 kW front and 340 kW rear motors, active suspension and rear-wheel steering.

legacy_notes.note: ET7 75 kWh launch version (2022). Legacy epa_range 207 is not an EPA figure (the ET7 is not sold in the US; WLTP is 445 km); current_price 88500 has no source or currency basis; acceleration_0_60 3.8 is Nio's 0-100 km/h time; generation '2023' should be 2022. The 2024 refresh is a separate generation row.

gaps: No yuan prices sourced for most current NIO trims (ES8 III, ES6/EC6, EC7, ES9, ET7 2024); the ES8 III pre-sale price (416,800 yuan) is not the launch price so it was left out.
Power and torque for the first-generation ES6 and ES8 are not reliably sourced per battery.
NIO's per-country European line-up in 2026 is unclear (registrations collapsed; EL8 only as certified used in Germany). EU market statuses are best effort.
ES6 second generation power output not in source used.
The 150 kWh semi-solid-state pack (rental only) is not modelled as a variant.
Five-seat ES8 (2026) is described but not modelled as its own variant (same powertrain).
